text:
Mina: Heads up: production kv slab memory spike on rtf-infer after today's runtime merge (commit abc123). Instances seeing OOMs ~10-15% higher :warning:
ci-bot: CI alert: perf/regression check flagged increased max RSS on perf-suite-kv by ~12% — https://ci.example/build/789
Sam: Thanks Mina. Any quick repro or flamegraphs? last green was before abc123 right?
Mina: Repro on staging is quick. Running the inference loop with long-context workload shows RSS climb:```ps aux | grep rtf-infer && pmap -x <pid> | tail -n 5
rtf-infer  1234  75.3 10.2  ...
00007f...   1200000    48000   1160000   80%```
Logan: I looked at the selector diff in abc123 — kernel-router now prefers fast-kernel-v2 for seqlen > 1024 due to the new heuristic. That kernel uses a different pagelet reservation path which touches a newer slab layout.
Infra-Anna: Is this coming from the kv caching heuristics change? PR 456 adjusted soft-prefetch / threshold tuning and landed with abc123 if I recall.
Mina: I bisected on staging: reverting PR456 returns RSS to baseline. Bisection notes: abc123 -> PR456 merged; revert of PR456 on staging reduces kv-oom rate from 0.12 to 0.01 over 30m.
Sam: If revert fixes it, do we need an immediate rollback to prod? What are the perf tradeoffs (p99, throughput)? Could autobatch or short-seq latency regress if we revert?
Logan: fast-kernel-v2 gives ~6% p99 improvement for short sequences but allocates larger pagelet reservations that increase fragmentation under long-context heavy workloads. So it's a regression for our long-tail memory usage.
Ryan: Proposed: fast rollback for hosted to stop OOMs, leave canary-only for Dedicated so customers can opt-in. Meanwhile add a feature-flag for kernel selector and work on allocator changes.
Mina: Working on rollback PR now: 355-revert-456. Tests passing on staging, running 1h soak.
ci-bot: Deploy bot: canary rollout started to 5% prod. Monitoring alerts: kv-oom-rate, slab_frag_metric, max_rss.
Infra-Anna: :thumbsup: Add short-term dashboards: 'kv/slab_rss', 'kernel/selection_counts', and an alert for slab_frag > 0.25.
Sam: Also add lightweight evict-debug trace: log evict window size + slab occupancy per request for a short period so we can correlate with seqlen distributions. Keep sample rate low.
Mina: Action items: 1) Merge rollback if soak looks good (Mina). 2) Profile fast-kernel-v2 allocator and pagelet reservation (Logan). 3) Add selector feature-flag + canary gating (Sam/Ryan). I'll post updates in 30m.
Logan: Pushed initial heap profile + allocator counters here: https://gist.github.com/xyz — shows increased reserved_pagelets and top hot path in kernel_alloc_reserve().
Mina: Thanks — please watch prod for OOM spike in next 30m and DM me if anything weird.
Sam: Will add the evict debug trace and a short-lived perf job to run longctx workload across kernels.
Ryan: If rollback lands, let's schedule a postmortem + plan: allocator fixes, selector guardrails, and a perf regression test for long-context memory.
Mina: Agreed. I'll update with soak result.
